blocks.text: You can provision users and assign predefined roles to them. Each predefined role has specific permissions that allow users to access and manage various modules in the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal.
Provisioning users and assigning roles provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Add and manage user accounts.
Manage and control users' access to the ITDR Admin Portal by assigning specific roles and privileges based on their responsibilities within the organization.
Leverage predefined roles and create custom roles with granular permissions to restrict user access to specific resources in the ITDR Admin Portal.
Manage user permissions easily by using repeatable role assignments.
Leverage user-role and role-privileges relationships to audit user privileges and implement changes quickly.

blocks.text: The following predefined roles are available:

table: This role has the highest level of privilege and has complete control over users, roles, APIs, modules, audit logs, etc.
Investigate events, block or add an attacker to an allowlist, and export logs.

blocks.text: In addition to the predefined roles, you can also create custom roles. You must have super admin privileges to add custom roles.
If you cannot add custom roles, then your organization has a standard subscription. Contact Zscaler Support to upgrade your subscription.
On the Users & Roles page (Settings > Users & Roles), you can see the following tabs:

blocks.item: Users
On the Users page (Settings > Users & Roles > Users), you can do the following:
View a list of configured users.
For each user, you can view:
Name: The name of the user.
Login ID: The email login ID of the user.
Contact Info: The email ID of the user.
Roles: The role assigned to the user.
Last Login: The last time (in days or months) that the user logged in.
See image.
Add a user.
You can add a new user account to the ITDR Admin Portal. Users can access and manage different modules in the ITDR Admin Portal based on the roles assigned to them.
To add a new user:
Go to Settings > Users & Roles > Users.
Click Add User.
See image.
In the User Details window:
Login ID: Enter the login ID of the user. It must be an email ID.
Email: Enter the email of the user. Emails to the user are sent to this address.
Name: Enter the name of the user. The name appears when the user logs in to the ITDR Admin Portal.
Disable Password Login: Select to disable the login process using a locally set password, but allow users to sign in via one of the single sign-on (SSO) options.
If this option is not selected, the Reset 2FA and Change Password options will not be available on the Account Settings page.
Blocked: Enable to block an existing user from accessing the ITDR Admin Portal.

Roles: Select one or more predefined user roles from the drop-down menu. The role defines the level of access the user has to the ITDR Admin Portal. If you assign more than one role to a user, then the user has permissions for all the configured roles.
Notify Only: Enable if you want the user to receive only email notifications and not access the ITDR Admin Portal.
Time Zone: Select a time zone from the drop-down menu. Alert timestamps are displayed according to the selected time zone.
Session Inactivity Timeout: Select a time duration after which an inactive user session is logged out. By default, this is set to 30 minutes.
See image.
Click Save.
The user is added and an email is sent to the user to configure the password.
See image.
If Authentication Service is enabled, you can't add users in the ITDR Admin Portal. You have to create users in the Authentication Service Admin Portal.
To configure users:
Go to Settings > Users & Roles > Users.
Click Add Users.
See image.
You are redirected to the Authentication Service Admin Portal.
Go to Directory > Users and add users and then assign the user to the Deception service. To learn more, see Adding Users and Assigning Entitlements to Users and User Groups.
Export user configuration details.
You can export the user configuration details as a CSV file.
To export the user configuration details:
Go to Settings > User & Roles > Users.
Click Export users (CSV).
See image.
A CSV file with the user configuration details is downloaded to your system.
Enable email alert notifications for a user.

You can enable email alert notifications to generate emails when a warning or critical event occurs in the ITDR Admin Portal. Email alert notifications help you to track specific activities, view event details, and take necessary actions.

Only super admins can enable email alert notifications. All users configured in the ITDR Admin Portal can disable email alert notifications for their account, but they must have super admin privileges to enable notifications.
To enable email alert notifications for a user:
Go to Settings > User & Roles > Users.
Locate the user you want, and click the Envelope icon.
See image.
In the Email Notifications Preferences window:
Enable Notifications: Select to enable notifications.
Under Fine-Tune Notifications:
License: Enable to generate email alert notifications when the license is about to expire.
Security Alerts: Enable to generate alerts when user settings are changed (e.g., when a password is disabled globally).
See image.
Click Save.
View user account activity information.
You can view activity information such as the number of failed login attempts, user creation time, user last login time, and user last password reset time.
See image.
Edit and delete a user.
You can edit or delete a user in the ITDR Admin Portal.
To edit a user:
Go to Settings > Users & Roles > Users.
Locate the user that you want to modify, and click the Edit icon.
See image.
In the User Details window, modify the required fields.
See image.

If Authentication Service is enabled, you can't edit the user details in the ITDR Admin Portal. You can edit only the time zone and session inactive timeout. You must manage a user from the Authentication Service Admin Portal. To learn more, see About Attributes.
See image.
Click Save.
To delete a user:
Go to Settings > Users & Roles > Users.
Locate the user that you want to delete, and click the Delete icon.
See image.
In the confirmation window, click OK.
A confirmation message appears to indicate that the user is deleted from the ITDR Admin Portal.
Roles
On the Roles page (Settings > Users & Roles > Roles), you can do the following:
View a list of predefined and custom roles.
For each role, you can view:
Name: The name of the role.
Description: The description of the role.
Users: The number of users who are assigned the role.
Permissions: The number of permissions or privileges the role has.
See image
Add a custom role.

In addition to predefined roles, you can add a custom role and configure permissions per your requirements. Based on the permissions configured for the role, users can access and manage modules in the ITDR Admin Portal.
Not all Zscaler ITDR subscription plans have privileges to create custom roles. You must have super admin privileges to add a custom role. Multiple roles can be assigned to a single user.
Go to Settings > Users & Roles > Roles.
Click Add Role.
See image.

If you get an error message after clicking Add Role that says custom roles are not available for your plan, then your organization has a standard subscription and you cannot add custom roles. Contact Zscaler Support to upgrade your subscription.
In the Role Details window:
Name: Enter the name of the role.
Description: Enter a description of the role. The description can include information about the privileges the role has, the purpose for creating the role, etc.
Permissions: Select the read or write permissions that you want to assign to this role from the drop-down menu.
The Read:ListUsers and Read:Appliances permissions are mandatory to access modules in the ITDR Admin Portal.
Users: Select the users to whom you want to assign this role.
You can leave this field blank and add the users later.
See image.

If Authentication Service is enabled, you can only configure a custom role, but can't assign it to any users. You must assign roles in the Authentication Service Admin Portal. To learn more, see About Authentication Service Admin Roles.
Click Save.
The role is added to the Roles table.
See image.
Edit or delete a role.
You can edit or delete a custom role in the ITDR Admin Portal.
You cannot edit or delete the predefined roles.
To edit a custom role:
Go to Settings > Users & Roles > Roles.
Locate the custom role you want to modify, and click the Edit icon.
See image.
In the Role Details window, modify the required fields.
See image.
Click Save.
To delete a custom role:
Go to Settings > Users & Roles > Roles.
Locate the custom role you want to delete, and click the Delete icon.
See image.
In the confirmation window, click OK.
IdP Providers

On the IdP Providers page (Settings > Users & Roles > IdP Providers), you can configure identity providers (IdPs) to support single sign-on (SSO) for users in ITDR. To learn more, see About Identity Providers.
See image.
Zscaler Remote Assistance
On the Zscaler Remote Assistance page (Settings > Users & Roles > Zscaler Remote Assistance), you can view the details of Zscaler Support users who can access the ITDR Admin Portal.
To view the support users' details, go to Settings > Users & Roles > Zscaler Remote Assistance.
The following support user details appear:
Name: The name of the user.
Login ID: The email login ID of the user.
Role: The role (Read-only or Admin) assigned to the user.
Created At: The number of days since the user account was provisioned.
Last Login: The last time (in days or months) that the user logged in.
See image.
Settings

On the Settings page (Settings > Users & Roles > Settings), you can configure user authentication settings and disable support users from accessing the ITDR Admin Portal. To learn more, Configuring User Authentication Settings and Disabling Support User Access.
See image.
